problem: Find the horizontal asymptote of $y=f(x)$ where $f(x)=\frac{2{x}^{2}+x-1}{3x+2}.$

activity_context.topic_title: Limits at Infinity and Horizontal Asymptotes of Rational Functions

examples.knowledge_point: Identifying When a Rational Function has No Horizontal Asymptote
examples.problem: Find the horizontal asymptote of $y=f(x)$ where $f(x)=\dfrac{x^5-10}{x^3-8x^2}.$
examples.worked_solution:
The horizontal asymptote is $y=\lim_\limits{x \rightarrow \infty} f(x).$ To find the horizontal asymptote, we apply the usual procedure of dividing the numerator and denominator by the highest power of $x$ in the denominator, which is $x^3.$

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to \infty }f(x) & ={lim}_{x\to \infty }\frac{{x}^{5}-10}{{x}^{3}-8{x}^{2}} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to \infty }\frac{(\frac{{x}^{5}}{{x}^{3}}-\frac{10}{{x}^{3}})}{(\frac{{x}^{3}}{{x}^{3}}-\frac{8{x}^{2}}{{x}^{3}})} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to \infty }\frac{({x}^{2}-\frac{10}{{x}^{3}})}{(1-\frac{8}{x})} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to \infty }(\frac{{x}^{2}-0}{1-0}) \\  & ={lim}_{x\to \infty }{x}^{2} \\  & =\infty .\end{aligned}
$$

The limit does not come out to a finite number. Therefore, there is no horizontal asymptote.

feedback.problem: Given that the horizontal asymptote of the function $f(x)=\frac{24{x}^{3}-1}{2c{x}^{3}-15{x}^{2}}$ is $y=-\frac{1}{3},$ find the value of $c.$
feedback.worked_solution:
The horizontal asymptote is $y={lim}_{x\to \infty }f(x).$ To find the horizontal asymptote, we apply the usual procedure of dividing the numerator and denominator by the highest power of $x$ in the denominator, which is ${x}^{3}.$

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to \infty }f(x) & ={lim}_{x\to \infty }\frac{24{x}^{3}-1}{2c{x}^{3}-15{x}^{2}} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to \infty }\frac{(\frac{24{x}^{3}}{{x}^{3}}-\frac{1}{{x}^{3}})}{(\frac{2c{x}^{3}}{{x}^{3}}-\frac{15{x}^{2}}{{x}^{3}})} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to \infty }\frac{(24-\frac{1}{{x}^{3}})}{(2c-\frac{15}{x})} \\  & =\frac{24-0}{2c-0} \\  & =\frac{12}{c}.\end{aligned}
$$

 

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{12}{c} & =-\frac{1}{3} \\ c & =-36.\end{aligned}
$$
